MECHANISM ATTEMPT (first non-knob of the session): static-shape cu_seqlens to remove the per-step torch.nonzero host sync from the ADOPTED fa3 varlen doc-masking path. Implemented behind DOC_MASK_STATIC_CU (default 0), echoed to RESOLVED_CONFIG, and verified byte-identical to the nonzero construction on the meaningful cu_seqlens prefix over 200 randomized trials before any GPU time. RESULT: REJECTED BY THE KERNEL. All 3 treatment arms died with 'CUDA driver error: an illegal memory access was encountered'; all 3 controls completed normally (0.929500/2009, 0.927866/1997, 0.928240/1990), which also confirms the edit did NOT disturb the adopted default path. FINDING: fa3 varlen does not accept a fixed-capacity cu_seqlens padded with zero-length trailing sequences. The kernel derives its sequence count from cu_seqlens.numel()-1, so declaring 8192 sequences against B*T=147456 rows of q/k/v drives per-sequence scheduling out of bounds. The 200-trial equivalence test proved the CONTENT correct and could not prove the CONTRACT -- content equivalence and kernel-contract compatibility are separate properties, and only the first is testable without the GPU. IMPLICATION: removing this host sync requires either (a) a capacity equal to the true document count, which needs the very host sync we are trying to delete, or (b) a kernel that accepts an explicit num_seqs argument separate from the cu_seqlens buffer length. Option (b) is the real proposal and points at FA4 / a custom varlen wrapper. The torch.nonzero sync therefore remains, and CUDA-graph capture remains blocked by BOTH this unbacked shape and the ~25GB graph-pool VRAM cost measured earlier.
